Every evening, millions of adult children ask, "Papa, medicines le liye?"Every evening, millions of adult children ask, "Papa, medicines le liye?"

The answer is always "Haan beta." But nobody can be sure. FIKR (फ़िक्र) is a concept app designed to ease this worry without making parents feel monitored.

The challenge

Five interviews surfaced two things:

  • Being asked can hurt more than taking the medicine
  • Routines often break during trips, illness or festivals

The approach

Parents tap one haldi button: Taken. The child sees silence when all is well, and a clear alert when something needs attention. FIKR turns everyday worry into quiet reassurance, without making parents feel monitored.

The details

  • One large "Taken" button, and one action per screen
  • Large type for older eyes
  • A bilingual interface with a spoken language option
  • A Material 3 design system with a night mode

Concept project. Persona photos are AI-generated. Music: "Classical Vibes 4" by Mixkit.

how it landed

OutcomeOutcome

A concept project, so these are the results it is designed for, not live numbers.

What I delivered

  • Research from five interviews, with affinity mapping
  • Personas, user flows and wireframes
  • A Material 3 design system with a night mode
  • Final screens and an After Effects film

How I’d measure success

  • Doses marked "Taken" each day, without a reminder
  • How often children open the app to check (fewer is better: silence means all is well)
  • Missed-dose alerts followed by a call the same day
  • Whether parents feel checked on less, in follow-up interviews

What it shows

  • Turning interview insights into one clear decision: a single button
  • Designing for older users: large type and one action per screen
  • A bilingual interface with a spoken language option
  • Motion used to tell the story
